text:
Priya: quick thread — running the next-samplekit starter + langchain eval harness I built and seeing intermittent 502s + duplicated downstream calls under moderate concurrency (10-20). repro steps in a sec.
Liam: ugh ok can you paste the minimal repro?
Priya: gist of the repro: spin up the sample on Vercel (edge runtime), run the eval harness which launches 18 parallel tests hitting /api/run-eval using the same session cookie. after ~30s we see ~20% 502s and a bunch of repeated invocation logs.
Priya: log excerpt:
```
INFO eval=42 request=118 handler=start session=sess-7
INFO http outbound=request id=118 url=https://hosted.api/redwood/generate
WARN sdk retry=1 reason=timeout request=118
INFO http outbound=request id=119 url=https://hosted.api/redwood/generate
ERROR upstream status=502 request=118 body="bad gateway"
INFO eval=42 request=120 handler=start session=sess-7
INFO auth refresh=start session=sess-7
INFO auth refresh=start session=sess-7
```
Priya: note two refresh starts for same session.
Anya: that looks like the classic edge-singleton caveat. our Node SDK added an internal refresh lock in v0.16 but the edge/wasm browser variant missed the parity change.
Liam: so the sample ends up creating the client per invocation which on edge can spin up multiple refreshes even inside the same worker.
Victor: minimal fixes: (1) update starter to export a singleton client from libs/redwoodClient.ts, (2) update sample README with edge-specific section, (3) add jitter/backoff and circuit-breaker in eval harness.
Priya: here's the singleton I dropped into the sample and it stopped duplicate refreshes locally:
```
// libs/redwoodClient.ts
import { Redwood } from 'redwood-sdk'
if (!globalThis.__REDWOOD_CLIENT) {
  globalThis.__REDWOOD_CLIENT = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
}
export default globalThis.__REDWOOD_CLIENT
```
Liam: nice — we should probably provide a small helper in the SDK that does this pattern so users don't copy/paste fragile global guards. maybe Redwood.singleton() that returns the same instance across imports.
Anya: agreed. I'll open an SDK parity PR to implement an internal promise-lock for refresh and a small helper for singletons in edge contexts. also will add docs explaining edge runtime nuances (module reload vs worker reuse).
Anya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/2040 (draft)
DevexBot: PR 2040 created by Anya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/2040 — CI: queued
Victor: quick note on retries in the sample harness: don't retry non-idempotent generate calls blindly. treat generate as "at-most-once" by default in the harness and use analytic reconciliation for failed evals.
Priya: good call. i changed the harness to mark failed evals and queue them for a single manual retry so we don't inflate token usage or create duplicate evaluations.
Liam: also adding a tiny e2e test that runs the eval harness with concurrency=20 for 60s and asserts failure rate < 5%. will add to sample CI.
Anya: checklist: SDK refresh-lock parity + singleton helper, update next-samplekit starter libs, README edge section, backoff + jitter example, harness change to avoid blind retries, e2e concurrency test.
Victor: timeline?
Anya: SDK draft today, sample PR tomorrow, follow-up README + CI later this week.
Priya: thanks — will attach the harness logs and a minimal repro to the sample issue. leaving notes for folks trying the starter on edge. :seedling:
Liam: ping me when the SDK helper is merged, i'll update other starter templates to use it. :eyes:
